headline: Michael Coelho selected to lead Massachusetts Trial Court administration
dek: The longtime Massachusetts Probation Service leader will become court administrator on Oct. 13, taking charge of statewide operations that support seven court departments and 94 courthouses.
body: The Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court has selected Michael P. Coelho as the next Court Administrator of the Trial Court, placing a longtime state-court manager in charge of the administrative system behind criminal, civil, housing, family and other proceedings across the Commonwealth. Coelho is scheduled to begin Oct. 13, according to the court’s Oct. 2 announcement. (https://www.mass.gov/news/supreme-judicial-court-appoints-michael-p-coelho-as-massachusetts-trial-court-administrator)

Coelho currently serves as deputy commissioner of programs for the Office of the Commissioner of Probation. The court said his portfolio includes the Massachusetts Probation Service’s work with specialty courts, the interstate compact unit, research, substance-use testing, reentry and sober-housing placements. Those responsibilities give him experience at the point where court orders, supervision and community-based services have to operate together, although his new job will be broader than probation administration.

He will succeed Thomas G. Ambrosino, who retired Sept. 18 after serving as Trial Court administrator. The change comes as the court system is managing its ordinary statewide responsibilities while continuing to modernize operations and support its workforce. Trial Court Chief Justice Heidi E. Brieger said Coelho’s government and probation background would bring a useful perspective to that work, while Coelho said he intends to continue advocating for the operational resources needed by court employees and users. The statements were included in the Supreme Judicial Court release; they describe priorities, not completed reforms. (https://www.mass.gov/news/supreme-judicial-court-appoints-michael-p-coelho-as-massachusetts-trial-court-administrator)

The administrator’s reach is substantial. The Massachusetts court system says the Trial Court is the largest component of the state Judicial Branch, with seven court departments, more than 6,400 employees and 94 courthouses. The administrator works with the chief justice of the Trial Court on the nonjudicial functions that let those courts operate, including budget preparation and oversight, labor relations, information technology, capital projects, security and personnel policy. (https://www.mass.gov/news/supreme-judicial-court-appoints-michael-p-coelho-as-massachusetts-trial-court-administrator)

The role was created by legislation enacted in 2011, and the Supreme Judicial Court’s FY2023 annual report describes it as a management post that supports the Trial Court’s delivery of justice rather than replacing the authority of individual judges. The report also identifies the administrator’s work as part of the court system’s broader organizational structure, where the chief justice and administrator coordinate operational decisions across departments. That division matters to the public: a leadership change can affect budgets, technology and facilities without changing the outcome of a particular case. (https://www.mass.gov/doc/fy-2023-annual-report-of-the-court-system/download)

Coelho previously spent three years as assistant secretary for policy and planning at the Executive Office of Public Safety and Security, where he also served as chief of staff, according to the appointment announcement. Earlier, he was a legislative director for former Gov. Mitt Romney. He holds a bachelor’s degree from Harvard College and a master’s degree in public administration from the Harvard Kennedy School. The court’s release also says he has more than 12 years in a leadership role at the Massachusetts Probation Service.

The immediate next step is the Oct. 13 transition. The appointment announcement does not set out a new strategic plan, funding package or timetable for specific operational changes. Those questions will become clearer through future budgets, court-system initiatives and public reports. For now, the confirmed change is a new statewide administrator with experience in probation, specialty courts and state government taking over a job that touches the infrastructure of every Massachusetts Trial Court department. (https://www.mass.gov/info-details/court-press-releases-2026)
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Michael Coelho named Massachusetts Trial Court administrator
seoDescription: Michael P. Coelho will become Massachusetts Trial Court administrator Oct. 13 after leading programs for the Massachusetts Probation Service.
